__notesAreHandWritten: `knownFailing` is regenerated from a real run; `notes` is hand-written and preserved across regeneration. Add a note whenever you add an entry — say whether it is a component defect or a limit of the sweep, and where the fix belongs.

notes.CnAddWidgetModal: COMPONENT DEFECT, inherited from a child. The warning surfaces here because CnAddWidgetModal renders CnIconBrowser (src/dialogs/CnAddWidgetModal.vue:87), and `this._uid` is a Vue 2 internal that Vue 3 REMOVED — it evaluates to undefined. There are five sites: CnIconBrowser.vue:357,367, CnIconBrowserPanel.vue:950,960 and CnPagination.vue:176. Each builds a DOM id (`'cn-page-size-' + this._uid`) used to pair a <label for> with its input, so on Vue 3 every instance on a page gets the SAME id (`cn-page-size-undefined`) — a duplicate-id and label-association defect, not just cosmetic. Fix: replace with a per-instance counter or `this.$.uid`. CnPagination does not surface it in this lane because its root v-if renders nothing under minimal props.
notes.CnAiAgentPicker: COMPONENT DEFECT. CnAiAgentPicker.vue:30-31 sets both `:input-label` and `:aria-label-combobox` on the same NcSelect; @nextcloud/vue 9 accepts only one. Fix: drop `:aria-label-combobox` (`inputLabel` already labels the control and is the accessible name). One-line change, deliberately left for a separate PR so this lane could land on its own.
notes.CnAiChatPanel: SAME DEFECT AS CnAiAgentPicker, surfacing through the parent — CnAiChatPanel renders CnAiAgentPicker in its #empty slot. Fixing CnAiAgentPicker.vue:30-31 clears both entries; remove them together.
notes.CnAppNav: COMPONENT DEFECT, accessibility. CnAppNav.vue:64 renders `<NcAppNavigation data-testid="cn-nav">` with neither `aria-label` nor `aria-labelledby`; v9 requires one so the landmark has an accessible name (WCAG 2.4.6 / 1.3.1). Fix needs a design call — a translated default like t('nextcloud-vue','Main navigation') versus a new pass-through prop — which is why it is not fixed here.
notes.CnAppRoot: LIMIT OF THE SWEEP, not a defect. CnAppRoot drives the whole app shell: it reads capabilities, resolves a manifest through async phases, and expects a router. Its seven dedicated specs each build that harness explicitly (five of them mock @nextcloud/capabilities per file). A generic minimal-prop mount cannot stand it up, and making the sweep do so would mean encoding one component's whole environment into a lane that is supposed to be uniform. Coverage lives in tests/components/CnAppRoot*.spec.js.
notes.CnDateRangePicker: COMPONENT DEFECT, and the most consequential one this lane found: the component is broken with its DEFAULT props. CnDateRangePicker.vue:224 declares `format` default `'YYYY-MM-DD'`. That was correct against @nextcloud/vue 8, whose NcDateTimePicker used moment.js; v9's uses date-fns, which REJECTS `YYYY` (year-of-week) where `yyyy` is meant and throws rather than warning. Fix: change the default to `'yyyy-MM-dd'` and sweep any consumer passing a moment-style format. Left out of this PR because it changes a public prop default.
notes.CnNotificationPreferences: LIMIT OF THE SWEEP, not a defect. The component calls @nextcloud/vue's `useAppSettingsDialog()`, which reads a provide() supplied by an NcAppSettingsDialog ancestor and returns undefined without one, so destructuring `registerSection` throws. It is only ever mounted inside that dialog in real use. A per-component spec that wraps it correctly is the right home for its coverage.
